items.followUp: A 0.20 kg stone moves in a circle of radius 2 m at 4 m s⁻¹. Find the tension in the string.

rubric.why: The mass must be converted to kilograms; the radius and speed are already in SI units.
rubric.description: States the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating m = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m and v = 5 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: The string tension provides the centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using T = mv²/r.

rubric.why: Correct substitution of the SI values is needed to calculate the tension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting m = 0.1 kg, v = 5 m s⁻¹ and r = 1 m into the formula.

rubric.why: The calculation gives a tension of 2.5 N.
The tension acts radially inward, toward the centre of the circle.
rubric.description: States the direction of the tension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the tension is directed toward the centre.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 100 g = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, v = 5 m s⁻¹.
Substitution: T = (0.1 kg)(5 m s⁻¹)²/(1 m).
The tension is 2.5 N, directed toward the centre of the circle.

items.followUp: A force has an x-component of 8 N and a y-component of 6 N. Find its magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: The perpendicular components combine according to the Pythagorean theorem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using R = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²).

rubric.why: The direction angle is found from the ratio of the y- and x-components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ = 5/12.

rubric.why: The angle calculated from the component ratio is approximately 22.6°.
Both components are positive, so the force lies in the first quadrant.
rubric.description: States the direction relative to the axes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force is directed 22.6° above the positive x-axis.

modelAnswer: Given: Fₓ = 12 N and Fᵧ = 5 N.
The force is 13 N at 22.6° above the positive x-axis.

items.followUp: What is a thermometric property? Give two examples of thermometric properties used in thermometers.

rubric.why: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a thermometer is used to measure temperature.

rubric.why: A useful thermometric liquid should expand uniformly as its temperature changes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liquid expands uniformly or regularly with temperature.

rubric.why: The liquid should be visible in the narrow thermometer tube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liquid is easily visible.

rubric.why: A suitable liquid should not wet the glass and should remain liquid over a wide temperature range.
rubric.description: States another useful property of the liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it does not wet or stick to glass, or that it has a low freezing point and a high boiling point.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
The liquid used in it should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should be easily visible in the narrow tube.
It should not wet or stick to the glass, and should have a low freezing point and a high boiling point.

items.followUp: A glass cube has side 4 cm and mass 150 g. If the density of glass is 2.5 g cm⁻³, find the volume of any cavity inside it.

rubric.why: The given side, mass and density are correctly converted to SI units.
rubric.description: States the data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting the side to 0.05 m, the mass to 0.306 kg and the density to 2550 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: The external volume of the cube is its side cubed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using side³ and obtaining 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.

rubric.why: The density relation gives the volume of the glass material.
rubric.description: Uses the density relation for the glass volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using Vglass = m/ρ and substituting the mass and density.

rubric.why: Dividing the mass by the density gives the volume of glass material.
The cavity volume is the external cube volume minus the volume of the glass material.
rubric.description: Finds and states the cavity volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for subtracting the glass volume from the cube volume and giving 5 × 10⁻⁶ m³ or 5 cm³.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 5 cm = 0.05 m, mass = 306 g = 0.306 kg, density = 2.55 g cm⁻³ = 2550 kg m⁻³.
Volume of cube = side³ = (0.05 m)³ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Volume of glass = mass/density = 0.306 kg/(2550 kg m⁻³) = 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Volume of cavity = volume of cube − volume of glass.
